     =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$

the isotropic oscillator with

$$
\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{0}=\frac12,\qquad 
\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2} .
$$

On the $m=2$ branch the Gauss–Manin period is $E$–independent.
With the normalisation ${\cal T}(0)=1$

$$
{\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad
{\cal T}'(\lambda)\equiv0,
$$

i.e. on the quadratic branch the hypergeometric factor is
identically $1$.  In the mechanical $2\pi$ normalisation
$T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}$

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}},\qquad 
T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi .
$$

Hence for the distinguished modulus $\alpha_{0}=\lambda_{0}=1/2$

$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\tfrac12)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
$$

and in the usual $2\pi$ mechanical normalisation

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}}
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda_{0}}}=2\pi\sqrt2 ,
$$

the constant harmonic period of $H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.
Removing the inessential $2\pi$ factor this is the normalised
real hypergeometric value ${\cal T}((n_{1}-1)/n_{2})={\cal T}(1/2)=
\sqrt2$, i.e. $T_{0}(1/2)=T_{0}(0)$ and in the $\pi$–normalisation
$T_{0}(1/2)=\pi$.  In particular the period is $E$–independent on
the $m_{1}=2$ branch, the familiar constant $2\pi/\omega_{1}$ of the
reduced oscillator.  Up to the conventional $2\pi$ factor this is the
quoted constant $\sqrt2$, $2\pi\sqrt2$ in the physical $T(0)=2\pi$
normalisation.  The formal degenerate labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2$,
$n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha^{f}=1/4$ gives the same constant normalised
period ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$, the ordinary
harmonic limit. ∎

2.text:
On the $q\mapsto -q$ $+$ eigenspace

$$
u_{r}(n)=\dim H_{+}^{1}({\cal C}_{E})=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}
n-1 &n\;{\rm odd}\\
n/2-1&n\;{\rm even}
\end{array}\right. ,
\qquad {\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n},
$$

so that $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ is the even generic value and
$u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the two odd neighbours.  Apart from the
formal degenerate $n=2$ limit the first non trivial even member is

$$
n_{1}=4,\qquad n_{2}=6,\qquad m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2,
$$

and $n_{k}=2k+2$ in general.  With the usual labelling

$$
\alpha_{0}:=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12 ,
$$

and

$$
\lambda_{1}=\frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{\,n_{2}-n_{1}\,}{n_{1}/2}}
        =\frac{2}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2}{2}}=\frac12 .
$$

On the $+$ eigenspace

$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
            =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda_{1}\bigr)q^{2}
            =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$

i.e. up to scale the harmonic oscillator with

$$
\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{1}=\frac12,\qquad 
\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}.
$$

For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss-Manin period is $E$–independent.  With the
normalisation ${\cal T}(0)=1$

$$
{\cal T}(\lambda)=\frac1{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}}
   ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad 
{\cal T}(0)=1,
$$

so that on the quadratic branch the ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor is identically
$1$.  In particular

$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\lambda_{1})^{-1/2}
      =\Bigl(1-\tfrac12\Bigr)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
$$

and with the conventional mechanical normalisation
$T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}$

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}},\qquad
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda_{1})=\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}}
     =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1/2}}=2\pi\sqrt2 ,
$$

the ordinary period $2\pi/\omega_{1}$ of
$H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.  Removing the inessential $2\pi$
factor this is the constant normalised real hypergeometric value
${\cal T}(1/2)=\sqrt2$, i.e. $T_{0}(1/2)=T_{0}(0)$ in the $\pi$–
normalisation $T_{0}(0)=\pi$.  In the $2\pi$–normalisation usually
quoted in the mechanics literature this is the familiar
$T_{\rm phys}\bigl((n_{1}-1)/n_{2}\bigr)=2\pi\sqrt2$, the constant
harmonic period on the $m=2$ branch.  The formal degenerate labelling
$n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$ gives $\alpha_{0}^{f}=1/4$ and the same
constant normalised period ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.
∎

8.text:
On the $q\mapsto -q$ $+$–eigenspace

$$
u_{r}(2k)=k-1=\frac n2-1,\qquad u_{r}(2k\pm1)=2k\pm1-1,
$$

so that $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ is the generic even condition and
$u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the generic odd condition on the two
neighbours.  Apart from the formal degenerate $n=2$ the first
non–trivial even pair is

$$
n_{1}=4,\qquad n_{2}=6,\qquad m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2,
$$

and $n_{k}=2k+2$ in general.  Put

$$
\alpha_{0}:=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12 ,\qquad
\lambda_{1}:=\frac{2}{n_{1}}
\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{\,n_{1}/2\,}}
      =\frac24\sqrt{\frac{2}{2}}=\frac12 .
$$

On the $+$ eigenspace

$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
      =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda_{1}\bigr)q^{2}
      =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$

i.e. up to scale the harmonic oscillator with

$$
\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{1}=\frac12,\qquad 
\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}.
$$

For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss–Manin period on the $+$ eigenspace is
$E$–independent and with the conventional ${\cal T}(0)=1$
normalisation

$$
{\cal T}(\lambda)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}}
      ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr) ,
\qquad {\cal T}(0)=1,
$$

so that on the quadratic branch the hypergeometric factor is
identically $1$.  In particular

$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\lambda_{1})^{-1/2}
      =\Bigl(1-\tfrac12\Bigr)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2 ,
$$

the constant normalised real period on the $m=2$ branch.  In the
usual mechanical $2\pi$–normalisation $T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}$,

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}},\qquad
T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi,
$$

hence

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}}
       =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda_{1}}}
       =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1/2}}=2\pi\sqrt2,
$$

the period $2\pi/\omega_{1}$ of $H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.
Removing the inessential $2\pi$ factor this is the normalised
hypergeometric value ${\cal T}\bigl((n_{1}-1)/n_{2}\bigr)={\cal T}(1/2)=
\sqrt2$, i.e. $T_{0}(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$ in the $\pi$–normalisation
$T_{0}(0)=\pi$.  Up to the conventional $2\pi$ factor the period is
the constant harmonic value, the formal degenerate labelling
$n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha_{0}^{f}=1/4$, giving the usual
${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$. ∎

5.text:
On the $q\mapsto -q$ $+$ eigenspace

$$
{\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n},\qquad 
u_{r}(n)=\dim H^{1}_{+}= \begin{cases}n/2-1&n=2k\\
n-1&n=2k+1\end{cases},
$$

so that $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ is the even condition and
$u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the two odd neighbours.  Apart from the
formal degenerate $n=2$ limit the first non–trivial even member is

$$
n_{1}=4,\qquad n_{2}=6,\qquad m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2,
$$

and in general $n_{k}=2k+2$.  Put

$$
\alpha_{0}=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12 ,\qquad
\lambda_{0}=\frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{n_{1}/2}}
        =\frac{2}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2}{2}}=\frac12 .
$$

On the $+$ eigenspace

$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{0}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
            =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda_{0}\bigr)q^{2}
            =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$

i.e. up to scale the harmonic oscillator with

$$
\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{0}=\frac12,\qquad 
\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}.
$$

For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss–Manin period on the $+$ eigenspace is
$E$–independent.  With the normalisation ${\cal T}(0)=1$

$$
{\cal T}_{m}(\lambda)={}_{2}F_{1}\!\left(\frac1{m-2},\frac12;
1+\frac1{m-2};\lambda\right)\xrightarrow[m\to2]{}
(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}={}_{2}F_{1}\!\left(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\right),
$$

so that on the quadratic branch the hypergeometric factor is
identically $1$.  In the mechanical $2\pi$ normalisation
$T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}$,

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\omega(\lambda)}
      =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}},\qquad 
{\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2},\qquad {\cal T}(0)=1,
$$

and ${\cal T}'\equiv0$ on the $m=2$ branch.  Hence
$\alpha_{0}=\lambda_{1}$ on the $m_{1}=2$ branch and

$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\alpha_{0})^{-1/2}
       =\Bigl(1-\tfrac12\Bigr)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
$$

i.e. up to the inessential $2\pi$ factor the normalised real
hypergeometric period is the constant $\sqrt2$, $ {\cal T}(\alpha)\equiv
{\cal T}(0)$ on the $m=2$ branch.  In the usual mechanical
$T(0)=2\pi$ normalisation

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda_{0}}}
      =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1/2}}=2\pi\sqrt2
      =\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}},
$$

the constant period $2\pi/\omega_{1}$ of
$H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.  Stripping the $2\pi$ factor this
is the familiar $\pi$-normalised constant $\sqrt2\,\pi$, i.e. the
$\pi/\sin\pi\alpha$ value $\pi$ at $\alpha=1/2$.  The formal degenerate
labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2,\;n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha^{f}=1/4$, gives the same
constant normalised period ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$,
the ordinary harmonic oscillator limit.  This is the minimal
$4,6$ even–odd pair and the constant harmonic period at
$\alpha_{0}=(n_{1}-1)/n_{2}=1/2$.
∎

6.text:
On the $+$ eigenspace of $q\mapsto -q$ for
${\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$ one has
$$
u_{r}(n)=\dim H^{1}_{+}({\cal C}_{E})=
\begin{cases}
n/2-1,&n=2m\\[1mm]
n-1,&n=2m+1
\end{cases},
\qquad u_{r}(2m)=m-1 ,
$$
so that $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ and $u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the generic
even condition.  Apart from the formal degenerate $n=2$ the first
non trivial even members are

$$
n_{1}=4\qquad n_{2}=6,\qquad m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2 ,
$$

and $n_{k}=2k+2$ in general.  In particular

$$
\alpha_{0}:=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12 ,
\qquad 
\lambda_{1}:=\frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{\,n_{1}/2\,}}
      =\frac24\sqrt{\frac22}=\frac12 ,
$$

so that on the $+$ eigenspace
$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
 =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda_{1}\bigr)q^{2}
 =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$
i.e. up to scale the harmonic oscillator
$\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{1}=1/2$, $\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}$.
For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss–Manin period on the $+$ eigenspace is
$E$–independent and
$$
{\cal T}_{\lambda}(E)=T_{0}\,{}_{2}F_{1}
\!\Bigl(\frac1{m-2},\frac12;1+\frac1{m-2};\mu E^{\frac m2-1}\Bigr)
\;\xrightarrow[m\to2]{}\;(1-\lambda)^{-1/2},
$$
so that in the normalisation ${\cal T}(0)=1$
$$
{\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
      ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad
{\cal T}'(\lambda)\equiv0 ,
$$
on the quadratic branch.  In the mechanical $2\pi$ normalisation
$T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}$,
$$
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}},\qquad
T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi,
$$
the ordinary $2\pi/\omega(\lambda)$ period of
$H_{\lambda}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac12(1-\lambda)q^{2}$.

Hence on the distinguished modulus $\alpha_{0}=\lambda_{1}=1/2$
$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\alpha_{0})^{-1/2}
       =\Bigl(1-\tfrac12\Bigr)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
$$
the constant $m=2$ value, and in the usual physical normalisation
$$
T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}}
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda_{1}}}
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1/2}}=2\sqrt2\,\pi ,
$$
i.e. $T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}=2\pi\sqrt2$ for
$H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.  Removing the inessential $2\pi$
factor this is the normalised real hypergeometric value
${\cal T}(1/2)=\sqrt2$, $T_{0}(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$ in the
$T_{0}(0)=\pi$ convention, the constant harmonic period of the
$m=2$ branch.  With the conventional ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation the
period is the constant $\sqrt2$, $T_{\rm phys}=2\pi\sqrt2$, and the
formal degenerate labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$ gives the same
constant ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$. ∎

9.text:
The $q\mapsto -q$ involution splits the Gauss-Manin system of

${\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$ 
on the $+$ eigenspace

$$
u_{r}(2k)=k-1=\frac n2-1 ,\qquad 
u_{r}(2k+1)=2k=n-1 ,
$$

so that $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ is the generic even condition and
$u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the generic odd condition on the two
neighbours.  Apart from the degenerate $n=2$ limit the first non
trivial even members are

$$
n_{1}=4,\qquad n_{2}=6 ,\qquad m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2,
$$

and in general $n_{k}=2k+2$.  With the formal degenerate labelling
$n_{0}=2,n_{1}=4$ one gets the formal first pair $2,4$.
Put

$$
\alpha_{0}:=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12 ,
\qquad 
\lambda_{0}:=\frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{n_{1}/2}}
          =\frac{2}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2}{2}}=\frac12 .
$$

On the $+$ eigenspace

$$
H_{\lambda}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
        =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda\bigr)q^{2},
$$

so that for the $4,6$ member

$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\tfrac12q^{2}\Bigr)
           =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$

the harmonic oscillator

$$
\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{0}= \frac12,\qquad 
\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}.
$$

For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss–Manin period is $E$-independent.  With the
conventional normalisation ${\cal T}(0)=1$

$$
{\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
   ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad 
{\cal T}(0)=1,
$$

i.e. the ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor is identically $1$ on the quadratic
branch.  In particular

$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\lambda_{0})^{-1/2}
      =\Bigl(1-\tfrac12\Bigr)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
$$

and ${\cal T}(\lambda)$ is $\lambda$–independent on the $m=2$ branch,
${\cal T}(\lambda)\equiv{\cal T}(0)$.  In the mechanical $2\pi$
normalisation $T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}$

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}}
      =\frac{2\pi}{\omega(\lambda)},\qquad 
T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi,
$$

hence for the distinguished modulus $\alpha_{0}=\lambda_{0}=1/2$

$$
T_{\rm phys}\!\left(\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}\right)
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda_{0}}}
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1/2}}=2\pi\sqrt2
   =\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}},
$$

the constant harmonic period of $H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.
Removing the inessential $2\pi$ factor this is the normalised real
hypergeometric value ${\cal T}(1/2)=\sqrt2$, i.e. $T(\alpha)\equiv
T(0)$ on the $m=2$ branch.  In the $\pi$–normalisation
$T_{0}(0)=\pi$ this is the constant $T_{0}(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$, often
quoted simply as the constant $1$ on the quadratic branch. The formal
degenerate pair $n_{1}^{f}=2,\;n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha^{f}=1/4$, gives
the same constant harmonic normalisation ${\cal T}\equiv1$,
$T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.  This is the $4,6$, $\alpha_{0}=1/2$,
harmonic case which is the unique minimal solution keeping the
Picard–Fuchs system on the $+$ eigenspace of rank $1$. ∎

public_text.10: Colleagues 1–9 have now converged on the same minimal even pair n₁=4, n₂=6 that simultaneously satisfies u_r(n)=n/2−1 together with the two neighbouring odd-order conditions u_r(n±1)=n±1−1. The explicit reduction of the given Hamiltonian after insertion of the square-root coefficient yields precisely the quadratic oscillator ½p²+(¼)q² whose frequency is 2^{-1/2}. public_text.7: The convergence on n1=4 and n2=6 across all prior contributions is decisive: it is the minimal pair satisfying ur(n)=n/2−1 together with the two neighboring odd-order conditions ur(n±1)=n±1−1, and the resulting λ1=1/2 reduces the given Hamiltonian exactly to the rank-1 quadratic oscillator ½p²+(¼)q² on the + eigenspace.      ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad

$$

     =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}},\qquad
T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi,

and in the normalised ${\cal T}(0)=1$ convention
${\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}$.

$$
{\cal T}\!\left(\alpha_{0}\right)
   =(1-\lambda_{1})^{-1/2}
   =\Bigl(1-\tfrac12\Bigr)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
$$

i.e. with the usual mechanical normalisation

$$

   =T_{\rm phys}\!\left(\tfrac12\right)
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda_{1}}}
   =\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}}=2\pi\sqrt2,
$$

the constant harmonic period of $H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.

normalised hypergeometric value ${\cal T}(1/2)=\sqrt2$, $ {\cal T}\equiv
(1-\alpha)^{-1/2}$ on the $m=2$ branch, viz. $T_{0}(1/2)=T_{0}(0)$,
which in the $\pi/\sin\pi\alpha$ convention is the constant
$\pi$.  The degenerate formal pair $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$,
$\alpha^{f}=1/4$, gives the ordinary harmonic normalisation
${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.  This is the $4,6$,

public_text.4:
The $+$-eigenspace of $q\mapsto -q$ on
${\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$ is

$$
u_{r}(2m)=m-1=\frac n2-1,\qquad u_{r}(2m+1)=2m=n-1 ,
$$

so that $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ is the generic even value and
$u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the generic odd value on the two
neighbours.  Apart from the degenerate $n=2$ limit the first non
trivial even member is

$$
n_{1}=4,\qquad n_{2}=6,\qquad m_{1}=\frac{n_{1}}2=2 ,
$$

and in general $n_{k}=2k+2$.  With the usual labelling

$$
\alpha_{0}:=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12 ,
$$

and

$$
\lambda_{0}
   =\frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{\,n_{1}/2\,}}
   =\frac{2}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2}{2}}=\frac12 ,
$$

the reduced Hamiltonian on the $+$ eigenspace is

$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{0}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
     =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda_{0}\bigr)q^{2}
     =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$

the isotropic oscillator with

$$
\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{0}=\frac12,\qquad 
\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2} .
$$

On the $m=2$ branch the Gauss–Manin period is $E$–independent.
With the normalisation ${\cal T}(0)=1$

$$
{\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad
{\cal T}'(\lambda)\equiv0,
$$

i.e. on the quadratic branch the hypergeometric factor is
identically $1$.  In the mechanical $2\pi$ normalisation
$T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}$

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}},\qquad 
T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi .
$$

Hence for the distinguished modulus $\alpha_{0}=\lambda_{0}=1/2$

$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\tfrac12)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
$$

and in the usual $2\pi$ mechanical normalisation

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}}
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda_{0}}}=2\pi\sqrt2 ,
$$

the constant harmonic period of $H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.
Removing the inessential $2\pi$ factor this is the normalised
real hypergeometric value ${\cal T}((n_{1}-1)/n_{2})={\cal T}(1/2)=
\sqrt2$, i.e. $T_{0}(1/2)=T_{0}(0)$ and in the $\pi$–normalisation
$T_{0}(1/2)=\pi$.  In particular the period is $E$–independent on
the $m_{1}=2$ branch, the familiar constant $2\pi/\omega_{1}$ of the
reduced oscillator.  Up to the conventional $2\pi$ factor this is the
quoted constant $\sqrt2$, $2\pi\sqrt2$ in the physical $T(0)=2\pi$
normalisation.  The formal degenerate labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2$,
$n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha^{f}=1/4$ gives the same constant normalised
period ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$, the ordinary
harmonic limit. ∎

so $T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=2\pi/\sqrt{1/2}=2\pi\sqrt2$, the period $2\pi/\omega_{1}$ of $H_{4}= \tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$. In the $\pi$ normalisation $T_{0}(0)=\pi$ this is the constant $T_{0}\equiv\pi$, i.e. $T_{0}(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$.

The $n_{1}=5,7,n_{2}=12$ Gamma proposals of round 0 are inconsistent with $u_{r}(2k)=k-1$ and with the requirement $m_{1}=2$ which forces the potential to reduce to a pure quadratic; they would give rank $>1$ and non-constant hypergeometric equations. Round 2 shows broad convergence on the $4,6$ pair and the constant harmonic period above. The degenerate formal pair $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha^{f}=1/4$, gives ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$, the ordinary harmonic limit.

Unresolved is the exact $2\pi$ vs. normalised ${\cal T}$ convention in the final statement; the invariant content is $\alpha_{0}=1/2$, $\lambda_{1}=1/2$, $\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}$ and constant period $\sqrt2$ in ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation, i.e. $2\pi\sqrt2$ in the usual $T(0)=2\pi$ mechanical normalisation.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The even $q\mapsto -q$ part of the Gauss-Manin system for
${\cal C}_{E}: y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$ is
$$
u_{r}(n)=\begin{cases}
n/2-1,&n\ {\rm even}\\
n-1,&n\ {\rm odd}
\end{cases},
\qquad u_{r}(2k)=k-1,\;u_{r}(2k\pm1)=2k\pm1-1,
$$
i.e. $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ and $u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the generic even
condition. Apart from the trivial degenerate $n=2$ limit the first
non-trivial admissible even numbers are

$n_{1}=4,\;n_{2}=6,\;m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2$, $n_{k}=2k+2$ in general.
The formal degenerate labelling is $n_{1}^{f}=2,\;n_{2}^{f}=4$.

Distinguished modulus
$\alpha_{0}=(n_{1}-1)/n_{2}=3/6=1/2$,
$$
\lambda_{1}= \frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{n_{1}/2}}
          =\frac12 .
$$
On the $+$ eigenspace
$$
H_{n_{1}}=\tfrac12\!\left(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{m_{1}}\right)
       =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac12(1-\lambda_{1})q^{2}
       =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2},
$$
the harmonic oscillator with $\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{1}=1/2$,
$\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}$.

On the $m_{1}=2$ quadratic branch the Gauss-Manin ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor
collapses to rank 1 and is $E$ and $\lambda$ independent:
$$
{\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
={}_{2}F_{1}\!\left(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\right),\qquad
{\cal T}(0)=1,
$$
and ${\cal T}'\equiv0$ on the branch.

Hence with ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation
$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\lambda_{1})^{-1/2}=(1-\tfrac12)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
$$
constant on the branch, and in the mechanical $2\pi$-normalisation
$T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=2\pi{\cal T}(\lambda)=2\pi/\omega(\lambda)$,
$$
T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=2\pi\omega_{1}^{-1}=2\pi/\sqrt{1/2}=2\pi\sqrt2 .
$$
In the $\pi$-normalisation $T_{0}(0)=\pi$ this is $T_{0}\equiv\sqrt2\,\pi$,
i.e. $T_{0}(1/2)=T_{0}(0)$; many authors quote the stripped
constant $1$ or $\pi$ for the normalised ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor.

The degenerate formal pair $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$ gives
$\alpha_{0}^{f}=1/4$, $\lambda_{0}=1$, the same constant normalised
period ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.

The minority Gamma proposals $n_{1}=7,5$ with $n_{2}=12$ etc,
$T\propto\Gamma(5/12)\Gamma(13/12)^{-1}$ etc., are inconsistent with
the $u_{r}$ formula and with the required $m=2$ degeneracy and are now
discarded by the majority. The remaining ambiguity is purely
conventional $2\pi$ vs ${\cal T}(0)=1$ vs $T_{0}(0)=\pi$ normalisation
of the real hypergeometric period. Stable content is $n_{1}=4,n_{2}=6$,
$\alpha_{0}=1/2$, constant harmonic period $\sqrt2$ normalised,
$2\pi\sqrt2$ in the physical $T(0)=2\pi$ normalisation.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The $q\mapsto -q$ splitting of ${\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$ gives on the $+$ eigenspace

$u_{r}(2k)=k-1=n/2-1$, $u_{r}(2k+1)=2k=n-1$,

so $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ iff $n$ is even and $u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the ordinary odd case. Apart from the degenerate formal limit $n=2$ the first non-trivial even numbers are $n_{1}=4,\;n_{2}=6$, $m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2$, with the formal labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$.

Hence

$\alpha_{0}=(n_{1}-1)/n_{2}=3/6=1/2$,

$\lambda_{1}= \dfrac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\dfrac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{n_{1}/2}}=\tfrac12$,

and

$H_{n_{1}}=\tfrac12\bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{m_{1}}\bigr)
        =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac12(1-\lambda_{1})q^{2}
        =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$,

a harmonic oscillator with $\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{1}=1/2$, $\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}$.

On the $m=2$ branch the Gauss–Manin ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor is trivial:
${\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}={}_{2}F_{1}(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda)$,
${\cal T}(0)=1$, i.e. the period is $E$- and $\alpha$-independent.
In the mechanical $2\pi$-normalisation $T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=2\pi/\sqrt{1-\lambda}$,
so that for the distinguished modulus

$T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=2\pi/\omega_{1}=2\pi/\sqrt{1-\lambda_{1}}
     =2\pi\sqrt2$,

and with the customary ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation

${\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\alpha_{0})^{-1/2}=(1-1/2)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2$,

i.e. up to the inessential $2\pi$ factor the real hypergeometric period is the constant $\sqrt2$, often quoted as the constant $2\pi\sqrt2$ physical period. In the $\pi/\sin\pi\alpha$ convention this is ${\cal T}(1/2)=\pi$.

The odd proposals $n_{1}=5,7$, $n_{2}=12$, $\alpha=1/3$ or $1/2$ with Gamma values $2\pi^{3/2}\Gamma^{-1}\dots$ are inconsistent with the $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ even condition and with the rank-1 $+$ eigenspace required for $m_{1}=2$; they are rejected by the majority in rounds 0–1 and Colleague 10 now concedes the $4,6$ pair.

The degenerate formal pair $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$ gives $\alpha^{f}=1/4$, $H=\tfrac12p^{2}+q^{2}/2-\sqrt2\,q$, $\omega=1$ and the same constant normalised period ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$, i.e. $T(1/4)=2\pi$ in physical normalisation, $\pi\sqrt2$ in the $\pi/\sin\pi\alpha$ normalisation.

Unresolved normalisation: literature quotes the value as $\sqrt2$ with $T(0)=1$, as $2\pi\sqrt2$ with $T(0)=2\pi$, and as $\pi$ with the $\pi/\sin\pi\alpha$ convention. The essential content is the constancy on the $m=2$ branch and $\alpha_{0}=1/2$, with the unique minimal even-odd pair $n_{1}=4,n_{2}=6$ satisfying the three consecutive $u_{r}$ conditions.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The reduced $q\mapsto -q$ even Picard-Fuchs order is
$u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ for $n$ even, $u_{r}(n)=n-1$ for $n$ odd. Hence
$u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ with $u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the generic even
condition. Apart from the formal degenerate $n=2$ limit the first
non-trivial even pair is $n_{1}=4$, $n_{2}=6$, $n_{k}=2k+2$, $m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2$.
The formal first pair is $n_{1}^{f}=2$, $n_{2}^{f}=4$.

With $n_{1}=4$, $n_{2}=6$

$\lambda_{0}= \frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{n_{1}/2}}=\frac12$,

$\alpha_{0}= \frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac36=\frac12$,

and on the $+$ eigenspace

$H_{n_{1}}=\tfrac12\!\left(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{0}q^{2}\right)
      =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac12(1-\lambda_{0})q^{2}
      =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$,

$\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{0}=1/2$, $\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}$.

For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss–Manin ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor collapses to rank 1
and is $E$- and $\lambda$-independent:
${\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
={}_{2}F_{1}(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda)$, ${\cal T}(0)=1$.
Hence on the quadratic branch ${\cal T}'\equiv0$.

In the ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation
${\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\tfrac12)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2$,
constant on the $m=2$ branch. In the mechanical $T(0)=2\pi$
normalisation
$T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=2\pi{\cal T}(\lambda)=2\pi/\sqrt{1-\lambda}
=2\pi/\omega(\lambda)$,
so

$T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=2\pi/\omega_{1}=2\pi\sqrt2$,

the ordinary harmonic period of $H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.
With the $\pi$-normalisation $T_{0}(0)=\pi$ this is $T_{0}(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$
and $T_{0}(1/2)=T_{0}(0)$ up to the $\pi/\sin\pi\alpha$ convention,
often quoted as the constant $\pi$ at $\alpha=1/2$.

The degenerate formal labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2$, $n_{2}^{f}=4$,
$\alpha^{f}=1/4$, gives the same constant normalised period
${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.

Colleagues 1–9,10 now converge on $4,6$; the earlier odd-$n$ proposals
$n_{1}=5,7$ with Gamma expressions are incompatible with the rank
formula $u_{r}(2m)=m-1$ and with the $m=2$ degeneracy required by the
square-root coefficient in the stated Hamiltonian. The only remaining
ambiguity is the conventional $2\pi$ vs ${\cal T}(0)=1$ vs
$T_{0}(0)=\pi$ normalisation, all of which give the same constant
harmonic value on the $m=2$ branch.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The $q\mapsto -q$ splitting of ${\cal C}_E:y^2=2E-q^2+q^{\,n}$ gives on the $+$ eigenspace
$u_r(2k)=k-1=n/2-1$ and on the whole space $u_r(2k+1)=2k=n-1$. Hence
$u_r(n)=n/2-1$ iff $n$ is even and $u_r(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ iff $n\pm1$ is odd.
Apart from the formal degenerate $n=2$ the first non-trivial even pair is
$n_1=4,\;n_2=6$ — $n_k=2k+2$ in general, with the formal labelling $n_0=2,
n_1^f=4$.  Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in both rounds converge on this; the
round-0 dissenting Gamma proposals $n_1=5,7$ with $n_2=12$ are now explicitly
dismissed as inconsistent with the even $u_r=n/2-1$ rank condition and with
the required $m=2$ degeneracy.

With $n_1=4$, $n_2=6$, $m_1=n_1/2=2$,

$\alpha_0=(n_1-1)/n_2=3/6=1/2$,

$\lambda_1=\frac{2}{n_1}\sqrt{\frac{n_2-n_1}{n_1/2}}=\frac24\sqrt{2/2}=1/2$,

so that on the $+$ eigenspace

$H_{n_1}= \tfrac12\!\left(p^2+q^2-\lambda_1q^{2}\right)=\tfrac12p^2+\tfrac12(1-\lambda_1)q^2
       =\tfrac12p^2+\tfrac14q^2$,

i.e. up to scale the harmonic oscillator with $\omega_1^2=1-\lambda_1=1/2$,
$\omega_1=2^{-1/2}$.

On the $m=2$ branch the Gauss–Manin ${}_2F_1$ factor is trivial,
${\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}={}_2F_1(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda)$,
${\cal T}'\equiv0$. In ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation

${\cal T}(\alpha_0)=(1-\lambda_1)^{-1/2}=(1-1/2)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2$,

constant in $\alpha$ and $E$. In the mechanical $T(0)=2\pi$ normalisation

$T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=2\pi/\sqrt{1-\lambda}=2\pi{\cal T}(\lambda)$,

hence $T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_0)=2\pi/\omega_1=2\pi\sqrt2$, i.e. $T_0(1/2)=\sqrt2\pi$
in the $T_0(0)=\pi$ convention and the common statement ${\cal T}\equiv1$ on
the quadratic branch.

The formal degenerate pair $n_1^f=2,n_2^f=4$, $\alpha_{01}=1/4$, gives the
same constant normalised period ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.

Normalization ambiguity remains the only unresolved point: the
literature quotes the normalised value $\sqrt2$ or $1$ after stripping the
conventional $2\pi$ factor, while the physical period is $2\pi\sqrt2$, and
in $\pi$-normalisation $T_0\equiv\pi$ i.e. $T_0(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$. The $4,6$
pair is the unique minimal non-degenerate solution keeping the $+$
Picard–Fuchs system of rank $1$ and reducing the potential to pure quadratic.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The reduced Gauss-Manin system on the $+$ eigenspace of $q\mapsto -q$ for ${\cal C}_E : y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$ gives

$u_{r}(2m)=m-1=n/2-1$, $u_{r}(2m+1)=2m=n-1$,

so $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ and $u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ iff $n$ is even, $n\ge4$.
Apart from the formal degenerate $n=2$ limit the first non-trivial even members are

$n_{1}=4,\; n_{2}=6,\; m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2$, $n_{k}=2k+2$.

Hence $\alpha_{0}:=(n_{1}-1)/n_{2}=3/6=1/2$.

With $m_{1}=2$

$\lambda_{1}= \dfrac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\dfrac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{n_{1}/2}}
        =\dfrac{2}{4}\sqrt{2/2}=1/2$,

$H_{n_{1}}=\tfrac12\bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{2}\bigr)
        =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac12(1-\lambda_{1})q^{2}
        =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$,

a harmonic oscillator with $\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{1}=1/2$, 
$\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}$.

On the $m=2$ branch the $+$ Picard-Fuchs operator is rank $1$ and the
${}_2F_{1}$ factor is trivial,
${\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}= {}_{2}F_{1}(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda)$,
${\cal T}(0)=1$, ${\cal T}'\equiv0$.  Hence the real period is $E$ and
$\lambda$ independent.

In ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation
${\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\lambda_{1})^{-1/2}=(1-1/2)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2$,
constant on the quadratic branch.  In the mechanical $T(0)=2\pi$
normalisation

$T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=2\pi{\cal T}(\lambda)=2\pi/\sqrt{1-\lambda}
      =2\pi/\omega(\lambda)$,

so $T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=2\pi/\omega_{1}=2\pi/\sqrt{1/2}=2\sqrt2\,\pi$.

Removing the conventional $2\pi$ factor this is the normalised value
$\sqrt2$, i.e. $T_{0}(0)=\pi\Rightarrow T_{0}(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$, and in
the $\pi/\sin\pi\alpha$ hypergeometric normalisation $T_{0}(1/2)=\pi$.
The formal degenerate labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha^{f}=1/4$,
gives the same constant normalised period ${\cal T}\equiv1$,
$T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.

Round 2 consensus: all colleagues now agree on the $4,6$ pair and reject the earlier Gamma proposals $n_{1}=5,7$, $n_{2}=12$ etc.; those would give higher order monodromy and do not satisfy the simultaneous three consecutive $u_{r}$ conditions nor the required $m=2$ degeneracy of the square-root coefficient in the quoted Hamiltonian. The only remaining ambiguity is the conventional $2\pi$ / $\pi$ / ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation of the period.

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The $q\mapsto -q$ split gives on ${\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$

$u_{r}(2m)=m-1=n/2-1$, $u_{r}(2m+1)=2m=n-1$,

so $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ and $u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ holds for every even $n\ge4$. 
Up to the formal degenerate limit $n=2$ the first non-trivial even
members are

$n_{1}=4,\;n_{2}=6$, $m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2$,

with the formal first pair $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$.  In particular

$\alpha_{0}:=(n_{1}-1)/n_{2}=3/6=1/2$,

$\lambda_{0}= \dfrac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\dfrac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{n_{1}/2}}
       =\dfrac{2}{4}\sqrt{2/2}=1/2$,

and on the $+$ eigenspace

$H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\tfrac12\!\left(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{0}q^{m_{1}}\right)
 =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac12(1-\lambda_{0})q^{2}
 =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$,

the harmonic oscillator $\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{0}=1/2$, $\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}$.
For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss–Manin ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor is trivial:

${\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
 ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\left(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\right)$, ${\cal T}(0)=1$,

hence ${\cal T}$ is $E$ and $\lambda$ independent on the quadratic branch.
Thus

${\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\lambda_{0})^{-1/2}=(1-1/2)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2$,

constant on the $m=2$ branch, i.e. ${\cal T}(\alpha)\equiv{\cal T}(0)$. 

In mechanical normalisation $T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi$,

$T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=2\pi{\cal T}(\lambda)=2\pi/\sqrt{1-\lambda}
 =2\pi/\omega(\lambda)$,

so

$T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=2\pi/\omega_{1}=2\pi/\sqrt{1/2}=2\pi\sqrt2$,

the period $2\pi/\omega_{1}$ of $H_{4}= \tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.
Stripping the $2\pi$ factor this is the normalised constant $\sqrt2$,
$\sqrt2\,\pi$ in the $T_{0}(0)=\pi$ convention, $\pi$ in the
$\pi/\sin\pi\alpha$ convention.

The earlier odd proposals $n_{1}=5,7$, $n_{2}=12$ with Gamma
expressions $2\pi^{3/2}(\Gamma(\dots))^{-1}$ are inconsistent with
$u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ requiring $n$ even and with the rank-one $+$
eigenspace required by the square-root coefficient; they are now
rejected by the consensus.  The dominant consensus in round 2 is the
$4,6$, $\alpha_{0}=1/2$, constant harmonic branch; the formal degenerate
labelling $2,4$, $\alpha^{f}=1/4$, gives the same constant normalised
period ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.  Normalisation
ambiguity $ {\cal T}(0)=1$ vs $T(0)=2\pi$ vs $T(0)=\pi$ remains, but the
$\alpha$-independence and the value $\sqrt2$ up to the conventional
$2\pi$ factor is stable. ∎

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The $q\mapsto -q$ splitting of $y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$ gives on the $+$ eigenspace
$u_{r}(2m)=m-1=n/2-1$, $u_{r}(2m+1)=2m=n-1$. Hence $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ and
$u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ iff $n$ is even.  Formally $n=2$ satisfies the three
conditions, $u_{r}(2)=0$.  Discarding the degenerate $n=2$ limit the first
non-trivial even numbers are $n_{1}=4$, $n_{2}=6$, $n_{k}=2k+2$.  With the
formal labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2$, $n_{2}^{f}=4$ the same constant
harmonic normalisation is obtained.

For the non-degenerate pair
$m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2$,
$\alpha_{0}=(n_{1}-1)/n_{2}=3/6=1/2$,
$\lambda_{0}=2n_{1}^{-1}\sqrt{(n_{2}-n_{1})/(n_{1}/2)}=1/2$.
On the $+$ eigenspace
$H_{n_{1}}=\tfrac12\bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{0}q^{2}\bigr)
          =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$,
$\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{0}=1/2$, $\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}$.
For $m=2$ the Gauss–Manin ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor is
${\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}={}_{2}F_{1}(1/2,0;1;\lambda)$,
hence ${\cal T}$ is $\lambda$– and $E$–independent on the quadratic branch.
In the ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation ${\cal T}(\lambda)\equiv(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}$
and ${\cal T}'\equiv0$, so

${\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-1/2)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2$,
$T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=2\pi{\cal T}(\lambda)=2\pi/\sqrt{1-\lambda}$,
$T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=2\pi/\omega_{1}=2\pi\sqrt2$.

In the $\pi$–normalisation $T_{0}(0)=\pi$, $T_{0}(\alpha_{0})=T_{0}(0)$,
i.e. $T_{0}(1/2)=\pi$, $ \sqrt2\,\pi$ in the $2\pi$ convention.
The $ \pi/\sin\pi\alpha$ ${}_{2}F_{1}(\alpha,1-\alpha;1;z)$ normalisation
gives the familiar value $\pi$ at $\alpha=1/2$.

Odd proposals $n_{1}=5,7$ with $n_{2}=12$ and Gamma expressions
$2\pi^{3/2}(\Gamma(5/12)\Gamma(13/12))^{-1}$ etc. are rejected: for odd $n$
$u_{r}(n)=n-1\ne n/2-1$, the $+$ eigenspace is not rank $1$ and the
square-root coefficient cannot produce the required $m=2$ degeneracy.
Colleague 10 now endorses the $4,6$ pair.

Unresolved is only the conventional normalisation factor: $2\pi\sqrt2$
physical, $\sqrt2$ with ${\cal T}(0)=1$, $\pi$ with the $\pi/\sin\pi\alpha$
${}_{2}F_{1}(\alpha,1-\alpha;1;z)$ convention, and the formal degenerate
labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2$, $n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha^{f}=1/4$, ${\cal T}\equiv1$,
$T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$. The mathematical content is the constant harmonic
period on the $m=2$ branch at $\alpha_{0}=1/2$.

\]

The classical action integral on the quadratic branch is likewise E-independent, confirming that the period cannot acquire the transcendental factors characteristic of higher-rank hypergeometric equations. The 4/6 reduction therefore supplies the unique solution consistent with both the monodromy data and the explicit Hamiltonian reduction.

1.text:
On the $q\mapsto -q$ $+$ eigenspace

$${\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n} ,\qquad 
u_{r}(n)=\dim H^{1}_{+}({\cal C}_{E})=
\begin{cases}
n/2-1&n=2m\\[1mm]
n-1&n=2m+1
\end{cases},\qquad 
u_{r}(2m)=m-1 ,
$$

so that $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ is the even generic value and 
$u_{r}(n\pm 1)=n\pm 1-1$ is the two odd neighbours.  Apart from the
formal degenerate $n=2$ limit the first non–trivial even member is

$$n_{1}=4,\qquad n_{2}=6,\qquad m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2,
\qquad n_{k}=2k+2, $$

and with the formal degenerate labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$.
On the $+$ eigenspace

$$\alpha_{0}:=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12,
\qquad 
\lambda_{1}:=\frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{\,n_{1}/2\,}}
      =\frac{2}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2}{2}}=\frac12 ,
$$

and

$$H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
     =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda_{1}\bigr)q^{2}
     =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2} .
$$

Hence on the $+$ eigenspace we have the isotropic oscillator

$$\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{1}=\frac12,\qquad\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}, $$

i.e. up to scale the harmonic oscillator.  For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss–
Manin period on the $+$ eigenspace is $E$–independent.  With the
${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation

$${\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
   ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad 
{\cal T}'\equiv0,
$$

so that on the quadratic $m=2$ branch the ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor is
identically $1$.  In particular

$${\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\lambda_{1})^{-1/2}
       =\Bigl(1-\tfrac12\Bigr)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
\qquad {\cal T}(\lambda)\equiv{\cal T}(0)
$$

on the branch.  In the usual mechanical $T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi$
normalisation $T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}$,

$$T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}}
      =\frac{2\pi}{\omega(\lambda)},\qquad 
T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi,$$

so that for the distinguished modulus $\alpha_{0}=\lambda_{1}=1/2$

$$T_{\rm phys}\!\Bigl(\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}\Bigr)
   =\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}}
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda_{1}}}
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1/2}}=2\pi\sqrt2,
$$

the constant period $2\pi/\omega_{1}$ of
$H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.  Stripping the inessential $2\pi$
factor this is the normalized real hypergeometric value

$${\cal T}\!\Bigl(\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}\Bigr)={\cal T}(1/2)=\sqrt2,
\qquad {\cal T}(1/2)={\cal T}(0),$$

i.e. $T_{0}(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$ in the $T_{0}(0)=\pi$ convention and
$T_{0}(1/2)=T_{0}(0)$ up to the trivial ${}_{2}F_{1}(\tfrac12,0;1;\cdot)$
factor.  In the formal degenerate labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2,\,
n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha_{0}^{f}=1/4$, $\lambda_{0}=1$, this is the
ordinary harmonic normalisation ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv
2\pi$.  This is the unique minimal $4,6$, $\alpha_{0}=1/2$ harmonic
branch on which the Picard–Fuchs system on the $+$ eigenspace is of
rank one. ∎

5.text:
On the $q\mapsto -q$ involution
${\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$ one has on the $+$ eigenspace

$$

$$

so that $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ is the even generic value and
$u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the two odd neighbours.  Apart from the
formal degenerate $n=2$ limit the first non-trivial even member is

$$
n_{1}=4,\qquad n_{2}=6,\qquad m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2,
\qquad n_{k}=2k+2,
$$

the formal degenerate labelling being $n_{1}^{f}=2,\;n_{2}^{f}=4$.
Put

$$

       =\frac{2}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2}{2}}=\frac12 .
$$

$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
      =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda_{1}\bigr)q^{2}
      =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$

i.e. up to scale the harmonic oscillator

$$
\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{1}=\frac12,\qquad \omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}.
$$

For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss–Manin factor on the $+$ eigenspace is

{\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
       ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad
{\cal T}'\equiv0,
$$

so that on the quadratic branch the hypergeometric factor is

$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\lambda_{1})^{-1/2}
       =\Bigl(1-\tfrac12\Bigr)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
$$

the constant $m=2$ value and ${\cal T}(\lambda)\equiv{\cal T}(0)$ on

T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}}
      =\frac{2\pi}{\omega(\lambda)},\qquad
T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi,

and for the distinguished modulus $\alpha_{0}=\lambda_{1}=1/2$

T_{\rm phys}\!\Bigl(\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}\Bigr)

4.text:
On the $q\mapsto -q$ $+$ eigenspace

${\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$,
$u_{r}(2m)=m-1=n/2-1$, $u_{r}(2m+1)=2m=n-1$,
so that $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ is the even generic value and
$u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ the two odd neighbours.  Apart from the
degenerate $n=2$ limit the first non trivial even member is

$n_{1}=4$, $n_{2}=6$, $m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2$,  $n_{k}=2k+2$,

and in the formal labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2$, $n_{2}^{f}=4$.
Put

$$
\alpha_{0}=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12 ,
\qquad 
\lambda_{0}=\frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{n_{1}/2}}
        =\frac{2}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2}{2}}=\frac12 .
$$

On the $+$ eigenspace

$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{0}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
 =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda_{0}\bigr)q^{2}
 =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$

i.e. up to scale the harmonic oscillator with

$$
\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{0}=\frac12,\qquad 
\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}.
$$

For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss–Manin ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor collapses to rank
$1$,

$$
{\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
      ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad
{\cal T}(0)=1,\qquad {\cal T}'\equiv0,
$$

so that the real action is $E$–independent on the quadratic branch.
In the mechanical $T(0)=2\pi$ normalisation
$T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}=2\pi/\omega$,

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}},\qquad
T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi,
$$

and on the distinguished modulus $\alpha_{0}=\lambda_{0}=1/2$

$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\tfrac12)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
$$

$$
T_{\rm phys}\!\left(\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}\right)
   =T_{\rm phys}\!\left(\tfrac12\right)
   =\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}}
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda_{0}}}=2\pi\sqrt2,
$$

the constant $2\pi/\omega_{1}$ period of 
$H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.  Stripping the inessential
$2\pi$ factor this is the normalised real hypergeometric value
${\cal T}\bigl((n_{1}-1)/n_{2}\bigr)={\cal T}(1/2)=\sqrt2$,
${\cal T}(\lambda)\equiv{\cal T}(0)$ on the $m=2$ branch, i.e.
$T_{0}(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$ in the $T_{0}(0)=\pi$ convention and
${\cal T}\equiv1$ in the formal degenerate labelling
$n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha^{f}=1/4$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.
This is the constant harmonic $4,6$ branch and the unique minimal
solution keeping the $+$ Picard–Fuchs system of rank $1$. ∎

3.text:
On the $q\mapsto -q$ $+$ eigenspace of
${\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$,

$$
u_{r}(2m)=m-1=\frac n2-1,\qquad u_{r}(2m+1)=2m=n-1 ,

so that $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ is the generic even value and
$u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the generic odd value on the two neighbours.
Apart from the formal $n=2$ limit the first non-trivial even member
with the two neighbouring odd members generic is

$$
n_{1}=4,\qquad n_{2}=6,\qquad m_{1}=\frac{n_{1}}2=2 ,
$$

i.e. $n_{k}=2k+2$ in general, the formal degenerate labelling being
$n_{1}^{f}=2,\;n_{2}^{f}=4$.  With

$$
\alpha_{0}:=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12,
\qquad 
\lambda_{1}:=\frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{\,n_{1}/2\,}}
      =\frac24\sqrt{\frac22}=\frac12 ,
$$

the $+$ reduction of the Hamiltonian is

$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
     =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda_{1}\bigr)q^{2}
     =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$

the isotropic oscillator with

$$
\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{1}=\frac12,\qquad \omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}.
$$

For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss-Manin period on the $+$ eigenspace is
$E$–independent.  With the normalised ${\cal T}(0)=1$ convention

$$
{\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
      ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad
{\cal T}'\equiv0,
$$

so that on the quadratic branch the ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor is identically
$1$.  In particular

$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\lambda_{1})^{-1/2}
      =\Bigl(1-\tfrac12\Bigr)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
$$

and ${\cal T}(\lambda)\equiv{\cal T}(0)$ on the $m=2$ branch.  In the
usual mechanical $T(0)=2\pi$ normalisation $T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}$,

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\,1-\lambda\,}}
     =\frac{2\pi}{\omega(\lambda)},\qquad T_{\rm phys}(0)=2\pi,
$$

hence on the distinguished modulus $\alpha_{0}=\lambda_{1}=1/2$

$$
T_{\rm phys}\!\left(\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}\right)
   =T_{\rm phys}\!\left(\tfrac12\right)
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda_{1}}}
   =\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}}
   =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1/2}}=2\pi\sqrt2,
$$

the constant $2\pi/\omega_{1}$ period of $H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.

branch on which the Picard–Fuchs system on the $+$ eigenspace is of
rank one. ∎

$$

On the $q\mapsto -q$ eigenspace
${\cal C}_{E}:y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$

$$

neighbours.  Apart from the formal degenerate $n=2$ limit the first
non-trivial even member with the two neighbouring odd members generic
is

$$

\qquad n_{k}=2k+2,

the formal degenerate labelling being $n_{1}^{f}=2,\;n_{2}^{f}=4$.

$$
\alpha_{0}=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12,
\qquad

$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)

i.e. up to scale the harmonic oscillator with

   ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr), \qquad

The convergence among colleagues 1–10 on the minimal pair \(n_1=4\), \(n_2=6\) is now unanimous and decisive. This is the first even index satisfying the three consecutive conditions \(u_r(n)=n/2-1\) together with the two generic odd-neighbour values \(u_r(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1\). Insertion of the square-root prefactor then yields exactly \(\lambda_1=1/2\) and reduces the Hamiltonian on the \(+\) eigenspace to the isotropic oscillator \(\frac12p^2+\frac14q^2\) whose frequency is \(2^{-1/2}\). On the \(m_1=2\) branch the Picard–Fuchs operator collapses to rank one, the hypergeometric factor \({}_2F_1(\frac12,0;1;\alpha)\) is identically 1, and the real period is therefore strictly \(E\)-independent. In the standard mechanical normalisation \(T(0)=2\pi\) one obtains the constant value
\[
T\biggl(\frac{n_1-1}{n_2}\biggr)=\frac{2\pi}{\omega_1}=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1/2}}=2\pi\sqrt2.
\]
Any candidate pair that produces a \(\Gamma(7/12)\Gamma(11/12)\) expression necessarily generates a Picard–Fuchs operator of order greater than one on the even subspace and therefore violates the explicit rank formula \(u_r(2m)=m-1\). The \(4/6\) reduction is consequently the unique solution compatible with both the monodromy data and the classical action integral on the quadratic branch.

=2\pi/\omega(\lambda)$,

and $T_{0}(1/2)=T_{0}(0)$ up to the $\pi/\sin\pi\alpha$ convention, often
quoted as the constant $\pi$ on the $m=2$ branch.

The degenerate formal labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2$, $n_{2}^{f}=4$,
$\alpha^{f}=1/4$, gives the same constant normalised period
${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.

The only remaining ambiguity is the conventional $2\pi$ vs

8.text:

5.text:

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The reduced $+$ Gauss-Manin system on ${\cal C}_E : y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$ under $q\mapsto -q$ is

$$
u_r(2m)=m-1=n/2-1,\qquad u_r(2m+1)=2m=n-1 ,
$$

so $u_r(n)=n/2-1$ and $u_r(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ iff $n$ is even.  Apart from the formal degenerate $n=2$ limit the first non-trivial even members with three consecutive generic orders are

$n_{1}=4,\;n_{2}=6,\;m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2$,  $n_{k}=2k+2$,

with formal degenerate labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$.

Hence

$$
\alpha_{0}:=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12,
\qquad 
\lambda_{1}:=\frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{\,n_{1}/2\,}}
      =\frac{2}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2}{2}}=\frac12 .
$$

On the $+$ eigenspace

$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
 =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda_{1}\bigr)q^{2}
 =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$

i.e. up to scale the isotropic harmonic oscillator with

$$
\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{1}=\frac12,\qquad \omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}.
$$

For $m_{1}=2$ the $+$ Picard–Fuchs operator is rank one and $E$–independent.  With ${\cal T}(0)=1$

$$
{\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
 ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad {\cal T}'\equiv0,
$$

so the ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor is trivial on the quadratic branch.  In particular

$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\lambda_{1})^{-1/2}=(1-\tfrac12)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
\qquad {\cal T}(\lambda)\equiv{\cal T}(0)\ {\rm on\ }m=2 .
$$

In the usual mechanical $T(0)=2\pi$ normalisation $T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}=2\pi/\omega$,

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda}}=\frac{2\pi}{\omega(\lambda)},
$$

hence

$$
T_{\rm phys}\!\Bigl(\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}\Bigr)
 =T_{\rm phys}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12\Bigr)=\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}}
 =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1/2}}=2\sqrt2\,\pi .
$$

Stripping the conventional $2\pi$ factor this is the normalised real hypergeometric value ${\cal T}(1/2)=\sqrt2$, i.e. $T_{0}(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$ in the $T_{0}(0)=\pi$ convention and $T_{0}(1/2)=\pi$ in the $\pi/\sin\pi\alpha\;{}_{2}F_{1}$ normalisation.  The formal degenerate $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha^{f}=1/4$ gives the same constant normalised period ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.

All colleagues in round 3 agree on the $4,6$, $\alpha_{0}=1/2$ pair and reject the earlier $\Gamma$-type proposals $n_{1}=5,7,12$ etc. which would require $u_{r}>1$ on the even subspace.  The only remaining ambiguity is the conventional $2\pi$ / $\pi$ / ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation of the period; the $m=2$ branch is constantly the harmonic period $2\pi/\omega_{1}$.

$u_{r}(2m)=m-1$, $u_{r}(2m\pm1)=2m\pm1-1$.  Hence $u_{r}(n)=n/2-1$ with
$u_{r}(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ is the generic even condition. Apart from the
formal degenerate $n=2$ limit the first non-trivial even pair is

$n_{1}=4,\;n_{2}=6,\;m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2,\;n_{k}=2k+2$,

with the formal degenerate labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2,\;n_{2}^{f}=4$.
All colleagues 1-10 now converge on this pair; the earlier odd-$n$
proposals $n_{1}=5,7$ etc. and the Gamma–expressions
$\,2\pi^{3/2}\bigl(\Gamma(5/12)\Gamma(13/12)\bigr)^{-1}$ are incompatible
with the rank formula $u_{r}(2m)=m-1$ and with the square-root coefficient
in the stated Hamiltonian.

For $n_{1}=4$, $n_{2}=6$

$\lambda_{0}= \frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{n_{1}/2}}=\frac12$,

$\alpha_{0}= \frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac36=\frac12$,

and on the $+$ eigenspace

$H_{n_{1}}=\tfrac12\!\left(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{0}q^{2}\right)
      =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac12(1-\lambda_{0})q^{2}
      =\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$,

$\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{0}=1/2$, $\omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}$.

For $m_{1}=2$ the Gauss–Manin ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor collapses to rank one
and is $E$- and $\lambda$-independent:
${\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
={}_{2}F_{1}(1/2,0;1;\lambda)$, ${\cal T}'\equiv0$.
Hence on the quadratic branch ${\cal T}$ is constant.

In the ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation
${\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\tfrac12)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2$, ${\cal T}(\lambda)\equiv
{\cal T}(0)$ on the $m=2$ branch.
In the mechanical $T(0)=2\pi$ normalisation
$T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=2\pi{\cal T}(\lambda)=2\pi/\sqrt{1-\lambda}
=2\pi/\omega(\lambda)$,
so

$T_{\rm phys}(\alpha_{0})=2\pi/\omega_{1}=2\pi\sqrt2$,

the ordinary harmonic period of $H_{4}=\tfrac12p^{2}+\tfrac14q^{2}$.
With the $\pi$-normalisation $T_{0}(0)=\pi$ this is $T_{0}(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$
and $T_{0}(1/2)=T_{0}(0)$ up to the $\pi/\sin\pi\alpha$ convention, often
quoted as the constant $\pi$ on the $m=2$ branch.

The degenerate formal labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2$, $n_{2}^{f}=4$,
$\alpha^{f}=1/4$, gives the same constant normalised period
${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.

The only remaining ambiguity is the conventional $2\pi$ vs
${\cal T}(0)=1$ vs $T_{0}(0)=\pi$ normalisation, all of which give the
same constant harmonic value on the $m=2$ branch. The consensus in round
3 is unanimous on $n_{1}=4$, $n_{2}=6$, $\alpha_{0}=1/2$, rank-one
collapse and constant period.

reflection_text.6:
The reduced $+$ Gauss-Manin system on ${\cal C}_E : y^{2}=2E-q^{2}+q^{n}$ under $q\mapsto -q$ is

$$
u_r(2m)=m-1=n/2-1,\qquad u_r(2m+1)=2m=n-1 ,
$$

so $u_r(n)=n/2-1$ and $u_r(n\pm1)=n\pm1-1$ iff $n$ is even.  Apart from the formal degenerate $n=2$ limit the first non-trivial even members with three consecutive generic orders are

$n_{1}=4,\;n_{2}=6,\;m_{1}=n_{1}/2=2$,  $n_{k}=2k+2$,

with formal degenerate labelling $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$.

Hence

$$
\alpha_{0}:=\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}=\frac{3}{6}=\frac12,
\qquad 
\lambda_{1}:=\frac{2}{n_{1}}\sqrt{\frac{n_{2}-n_{1}}{\,n_{1}/2\,}}
      =\frac{2}{4}\sqrt{\frac{2}{2}}=\frac12 .
$$

On the $+$ eigenspace

$$
H_{n_{1}}(p,q)=\frac12\Bigl(p^{2}+q^{2}-\lambda_{1}q^{m_{1}}\Bigr)
 =\frac12p^{2}+\frac12\bigl(1-\lambda_{1}\bigr)q^{2}
 =\frac12p^{2}+\frac14q^{2},
$$

i.e. up to scale the isotropic harmonic oscillator with

$$
\omega_{1}^{2}=1-\lambda_{1}=\frac12,\qquad \omega_{1}=2^{-1/2}.
$$

For $m_{1}=2$ the $+$ Picard–Fuchs operator is rank one and $E$–independent.  With ${\cal T}(0)=1$

$$
{\cal T}(\lambda)=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}
 ={}_{2}F_{1}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12,0;1;\lambda\Bigr),\qquad {\cal T}'\equiv0,
$$

so the ${}_{2}F_{1}$ factor is trivial on the quadratic branch.  In particular

$$
{\cal T}(\alpha_{0})=(1-\lambda_{1})^{-1/2}=(1-\tfrac12)^{-1/2}=\sqrt2,
\qquad {\cal T}(\lambda)\equiv{\cal T}(0)\ {\rm on\ }m=2 .
$$

In the usual mechanical $T(0)=2\pi$ normalisation $T_{\rm phys}=2\pi{\cal T}=2\pi/\omega$,

$$
T_{\rm phys}(\lambda)=\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1-\lambda}}=\frac{2\pi}{\omega(\lambda)},
$$

hence

$$
T_{\rm phys}\!\Bigl(\frac{n_{1}-1}{n_{2}}\Bigr)
 =T_{\rm phys}\!\Bigl(\tfrac12\Bigr)=\frac{2\pi}{\omega_{1}}
 =\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt{1/2}}=2\sqrt2\,\pi .
$$

Stripping the conventional $2\pi$ factor this is the normalised real hypergeometric value ${\cal T}(1/2)=\sqrt2$, i.e. $T_{0}(1/2)=\sqrt2\,\pi$ in the $T_{0}(0)=\pi$ convention and $T_{0}(1/2)=\pi$ in the $\pi/\sin\pi\alpha\;{}_{2}F_{1}$ normalisation.  The formal degenerate $n_{1}^{f}=2,n_{2}^{f}=4$, $\alpha^{f}=1/4$ gives the same constant normalised period ${\cal T}\equiv1$, $T_{\rm phys}\equiv2\pi$.

All colleagues in round 3 agree on the $4,6$, $\alpha_{0}=1/2$ pair and reject the earlier $\Gamma$-type proposals $n_{1}=5,7,12$ etc. which would require $u_{r}>1$ on the even subspace.  The only remaining ambiguity is the conventional $2\pi$ / $\pi$ / ${\cal T}(0)=1$ normalisation of the period; the $m=2$ branch is constantly the harmonic period $2\pi/\omega_{1}$.
